message.content:
# KIMI K3 — ROUND 3

## Framing corrections first

Two. (1) **O2:** the matrix asks whether disclosure "satisfies" me, but my R2 move to Y′ was instrumental — I wanted the correct-but-late penalty *visible*, and Claude's own withdrawal of Y′ plus the disclosure line achieves that. The secretary's question is answered by its own party's text. (2) **S8:** I never explicitly confirmed Claude's scoping of my n_obs alarm to refit events. I confirm it now: my bare version would have fired monthly under the frozen cadence I myself proposed. The scoped version is strictly better.

## O1 — Row universe

My common-mask demand was never about the mask; it was the guarantee that any printed gate number sits on identical origins with no pairwise samples. Claude's compromise delivers that guarantee via the loud assertion while removing the CAPE-hostage failure mode — strictly better than my R2 position. **Live with it**, two conditions made explicit: assertion failure is a hard error (no gate number, prints "comparison unavailable"), and the manifest records per-model estimation end and n_obs so a divergent-sample operational estimate is identifiable from the ledger hash. No veto.

## O2 — Oracle-free label

Disclosure satisfies the 2008Q2 concern **only if** the supplement prints twice: all live-publishable origins, and excluding the flagged in-recession-but-unannounced origins — not merely their count. Gemini's steepening argument is decisive against Y′ as a *scored* label: in month 6 of a recession the curve has re-steepened, P≈5 %, and scoring that against Y′=1 manufactures structural negative skill for a correct onset read. **Live with:** strict onset label, real-time censoring, maturity floor, identical baseline coverage, two-variant print. **VETO:** any scored use of Y′. Evidence that flips me: a walk-forward demonstration that a curve-based onset model keeps positive skill under Y′ — mechanically near-impossible given the steepening, so treat this veto as close to final.

## O3 — NBER-triggered refit

This is my R2 proposal with September named; the versioned-event requirement is precisely what separates a trigger from a silent refit, which is Astra's actual objection. **Live with it.** The trigger must be a hash change in committed `nber_announcements.csv` (new peak or trough), never a data refresh; the bridge row prints P under both weight vectors at identical inputs. No veto.

## O4 — Paired-rule endgame

The proposed resolution *is* my position: the backtest now was my core demand, because two live origins cannot estimate a disagreement rate; the 12-month parallel run happens anyway through monthly supplement printing. **Live with it**, backtest specification fixed: both rules applied to the same walk-forward origins with the same bootstrap draws, disagreement count and the disagreeing origins published. **VETO:** any automatic verdict-rule migration in this release — already excluded, and the README must say so in one sentence.

## O5 — Direction prediction

Accept; the staged bridge makes the prediction cleanly falsifiable. Stating it now: adding 2023Q3–2024Q1 (deep inversion, no onset) makes β_curve less negative, reduces extended-panel skill relative to the truncated panel's +34.3 %, and lowers P at fixed inputs. Astra's caveat is correct — the third holds only net of intercept and standardisation shifts — which is exactly why the fixed-input bridge is the test. No veto.

## O6 — CAPE outlier guards

The flag override is my hard guard with a paper trail: no silent garbage, no permanent block in a real crash. **Live with it**, one addition: `--accept-outlier` use goes in the ledger **note column**, not only meta.json — the ledger is the public record. No veto.

## O7 — Anchor month

September. My rolling-12 was always equivalent after the first cycle.

## Vetoes, consolidated

Two live: scored Y′ (O2); automatic verdict-rule migration (O4). One conditional: any weakening of O1's loud assertion to a warning footnote. Everything else in the matrix I sign.

## On Claude's draft as a whole

With O1–O7 resolved as above, the five-point plan is approvable. Its original defect — "publish whatever comes out" with no pre-stated expectation — is repaired by O5. The plan survives scrutiny; the spine bug it fixes survived nine months of Claude's own ritual. That asymmetry is the lesson, and S9's staleness guard is its price.

The task: for each OPEN dispute (O1–O7), give final position in 1–2 sentences, then the compromise I can live with. Mark vetoes and evidence that would change my mind. Challenge the secretary's framing if it misrepresents me. Don't reopen settled points. ~600 words hard limit.

O1 — Row universe. Secretary says: "Kimi: common mask; pairwise intersections mean up to 28 evaluation samples with no MDE; zero origins gained." That's accurate to my Round 2 position. Claude's compromise: start fixed as protocol constant, end set by each model's own features + label, gate requires identical origins and fails loudly otherwise. In practice today, with the spine fixed, all features run to 2026-09, so the end is the same for all models — the assertion passes trivially. The compromise only matters if multpl breaks. Does it give me what I want? My key demands: no pairwise samples, no dual estimates, gate on identical origins. Claude's compromise delivers: gate requires identical origins, fails loudly. The estimation end differs only when data availability differs — in which case a common mask would either truncate everything (holding curve-only hostage to CAPE) or... Actually under my common mask, if multpl breaks, the whole panel truncates, including curve-only. Under Claude's compromise, curve-only keeps running and the gate prints "comparison unavailable." That's arguably better than my position and preserves the audit guarantee I care about: any printed gate number is on identical origins. So I can accept it. But I should note one condition: the legacy replay (S2) requires the start fixed at 1947Q2 — the compromise does that. And I should insist that when the assertion fails, the operational model's own estimation sample is still reported with n_obs and train-end in the manifest, so the ledger remains interpretable. Also: the published +34.3% was estimated on the common sample; under the compromise, if samples diverge, the skill number printed must be the common-sample one or clearly labeled. Actually the compromise says gate fails loudly — no number printed. Fine.

One more check: does the compromise change the truncation regression test? The legacy replay uses frozen Yale inputs through the old chain — start 1947Q2 fixed, so it reproduces w and n_obs=264. Good.

So O1: accept Claude's compromise. Not a veto point. Condition: the "fails loudly" state must be a hard error in the gate output, not a footnote; and the manifest records each model's estimation end.

O2 — Oracle-free supplement label. Secretary says I moved to Y′ in R2, and the proposed resolution is strict onset label + real-time censoring, plus a printed line counting in-recession-but-unannounced origins scored and their loss contribution. Question to me: does disclosure satisfy the 2008Q2 concern, or do I veto?

My R2 position: I conceded Claude's Y′ because "2008Q2-type origins are scored as misses that live users experienced as hits." Claude then withdrew Y′ in its own R2 position (interesting — the matrix says Claude R2 proposed strict label; Claude's own position text says "I withdraw my Y′ label. My concern was that origins inside an unannounced recession get scored against Y=0 (no new onset within 4 quarters, since the recession is ongoing) and the model's elevated P looks like a miss. Wait — actually let me think carefully. 2008Q2: recession started Dec 2007 (peak), announced Dec 2008. An origin at 2008Q2: is there a new onset within the next 4 quarters? No — the recession is already ongoing; the onset was 2007Q4. So Y=0 for the onset label. Under real-time censoring as of the origin date: at 2008Q2, the announcement table as of that date doesn't include the 2007Q4 peak (announced Dec 2008), so this origin is NOT censored in real time — it was live-publishable. The model at 2008Q2: curve had been steepening after the 2006-07 inversion... actually by 2008Q2 the curve was positive. Hmm, but the model's P might still be elevated or not. The point is: the origin is scored against Y=0, and if P was elevated, it's a "miss" that a live user experienced as a hit (recession was underway).

Under the strict label with real-time censoring, that origin IS scored (it was live-publishable) against Y=0. My concern was that this penalizes the model for being right. The disclosure line makes the penalty visible: count of in-recession-but-unannounced origins and their loss contribution.

The alternative Y′ changes the estimand and Gemini's structural-negative-skill argument is strong: in month 6 of a recession the curve has re-steepened, P≈5%, scored against Y′=1 → massive penalty for a correct onset read. That's decisive against Y′ as a scored label. My 2008Q2 concern is really about interpretation, and disclosure addresses interpretation without corrupting the estimand. Also note: this is a supplementary score, not the verdict. So yes, I can accept disclosure. I should not veto. Actually, better: I can ask that the disclosure line include the loss contribution excluding those origins too — i.e., print the supplementary score with and without the in-recession-unannounced origins. That's a cheap addition and fully resolves my concern: two numbers, both computed, reader sees both. Let me propose that as my acceptable compromise: strict label + censoring + the score printed both including and excluding the flagged origins. That's stronger than "count and loss contribution" and costs three lines of code.

O3 — NBER-triggered refit. My R2 position: refit on NBER-table change or 12 months elapsed, whichever first. That's exactly my position with September as the month. Accept. Astra's concern is silent/automatic refits; the versioned-event requirement addresses it. That's my position minus the 12-month parallel requirement... actually it includes the backtest now, which was my key demand ("two live origins cannot estimate a disagreement rate"). The 12-month parallel run still happens de facto since the supplement is printed monthly. Accept. No veto. I might add: the backtest must apply both rules to the historical ledger-equivalent origins (the walk-forward scored origins), using the same bootstrap draws, and report the disagreement count and which origins disagreed. With ~50-70 scored origins, the disagreement rate will be noisy but informative.

O5 — Direction prediction. Proposed resolution: README states my expected direction before the run, labeled falsifiable with Astra's caveat, bridge table shows outcome. That's exactly what I wanted plus Astra's caveat, which is legitimate. Accept. I should restate the prediction precisely so it's falsifiable: extending the panel to include 2023Q3–2024Q1 (deep inversion, no onset) will (a) make β_curve less negative, (b) reduce walk-forward skill on the extended panel relative to +34.3% on the truncated panel, (c) lower current P relative to what the same inputs would have produced under the old weights. Astra's caveat: (c) holds only if intercept/standardisation/sample effects don't dominate; the bridge at fixed inputs isolates the weight change. Good — the staged bridge (S7) actually makes (c) testable cleanly: same input vector, old weights vs new weights. So my prediction is falsifiable on the bridge row alone.

O6 — Outlier guards on CAPE. My R2: level 5–60 and m/m <15% as hard guards. Proposed resolution: guard fails the snapshot unless rerun with --accept-outlier flag recorded in meta.json. That's a hard guard with an override that leaves a paper trail — it satisfies my intent (no silent garbage) and Astra's (no automatic rejection of genuine crashes). Accept. One condition: the flag's use must also appear in the ledger note column for that month, not only meta.json — the ledger is the public-facing record. Cheap.

O7 — Anchor month: September. I already noted my rolling-12 collapses to September after the first one. Accept, trivial.

Now — the secretary's framing check. Did the matrix misrepresent me anywhere?

1. O2: "Kimi (moved to Y′ in R2)" — accurate as of R2, but the matrix omits that Claude itself withdrew Y′ in its own R2 text, so the "proposed resolution" attributes to me a veto question that's already moot. I should note the framing is fine but the question is answered by Claude's own withdrawal; I follow the same logic. Actually the matrix does present the proposed resolution as strict label + disclosure, and asks me whether disclosure satisfies. So framing is okay. But I could note: my move to Y′ was conditional on it being the only way to make the "correct but late" penalty visible; Claude's withdrawal plus the disclosure line achieves the same end without corrupting the estimand. So no misrepresentation, but worth one sentence.

2. S6: "Gemini conceded in Round 2" — accurate.

3. S3: manifest — I adopted Astra's manifest in R2; matrix says settled. Fine.

4. O1: "Kimi: common mask... zero origins gained." Accurate. But one nuance: my "zero origins gained" was conditional on the spine fix. The matrix states it flatly. Fine.

5. The matrix's S8 says "n_obs must grow by exactly the audited number of new origins, else fail (this replaces the bare 'weights must change' alarm)" — that was my alarm, scoped by Claude to refit events, which I accepted implicitly? In R2 I said "Scope it to refit events" was Claude's attack on me... Actually Claude attacked my Q7(i) and I didn't respond in R2 to that scoping. The matrix declares it settled. Is it acceptable? Yes — the scoped version is strictly better; the bare version would fire monthly under frozen cadence. I'll explicitly confirm S8's scoped alarm to remove doubt, since the matrix marks it settled and I never explicitly said so. One sentence.

- O2: I'd veto Y′ if it resurfaces as a *scored* label (Gemini's structural negative skill argument). - O1: I'd veto any version where a printed gate number comes from non-identical origin sets (silent sample mismatch). The compromise's "fails loudly" satisfies me; if "fails loudly" is weakened to a warning footnote, I veto.

I'll state my condition as: the loud failure must be a hard error in the gate step and the manifest must record per-model estimation end — both already implied, I want them explicit.
